title: Linked List Cycle II
contract: Build a list whose tail points to input index pos, or no cycle for pos=−1. Return the cycle entry index, or −1.
brute: Node[] nodes=cycleList(input,pos);Node head=nodes.length==0?null:nodes[0];Set<Node> seen=new HashSet<>();for(Node node=head;node!=null;node=node.next){emit("Record a node identity","value",node.value);if(!seen.add(node)){for(int i=0;i<nodes.length;i++)if(nodes[i]==node)return i;}}return -1;
optimal: Node[] nodes=cycleList(input,pos);Node head=nodes.length==0?null:nodes[0],slow=head,fast=head;while(fast!=null&&fast.next!=null){slow=slow.next;fast=fast.next.next;emit("Search for a meeting","slow value",slow.value,"fast value",fast==null?null:fast.value);if(slow==fast){slow=head;while(slow!=fast){slow=slow.next;fast=fast.next;emit("Locate the entry","value",slow.value);}for(int i=0;i<nodes.length;i++)if(nodes[i]==slow)return i;}}return -1;
reasoning: A repeated node identity, not a repeated value, proves a cycle.
Within a cycle, a two-speed pair eventually meets. Resetting one pointer to the head makes equal-speed movement meet at the entry.
Check fast and fast.next before dereferencing. Entry-index lookup and graph construction are demo conversions; Floyd's traversal itself uses constant auxiliary space.
complexity: O(n), O(1) traversal auxiliary excluding input conversion
